The Cadet Warrant Officer of Central Area (WOCA) is a senior cadet appointment within the New Zealand Cadet Forces (NZCF), serving as the principal cadet advisor for the Central Area. The role exists to provide guidance on matters affecting cadet personnel, training, welfare, and general cadet experience across the region.
The WOCA is a supplementary member of the Central Area Cadet Forces Training and Support Unit (CA CFTSU) and works closely with the Area Commander and Area Support Officers. As the most senior Cadet Warrant Officer in the Central Area, the WOCA represents cadet perspectives at both strategic and operational levels within NZCF.
The position is tri-corps, representing cadets from the Sea Cadet Corps, New Zealand Cadet Corps, and Air Training Corps.
Roles & Responsibilities
The WOCA is responsible for:
* Advising on matters relating to cadet welfare, training standards, and organisational practice within Central Area.
* Acting as the senior cadet representative for the region and providing a link between cadet units and NZCF leadership.
* Supporting communication and coordination between units, Area staff, and national headquarters.
* Contributing cadet insights to strategic discussions and decisions that affect the NZCF as a whole.
* Supporting public understanding of the NZCF through engagement with community groups and stakeholders when required
* Maintaining professional relationships with cadets, staff, and stakeholders across all three NZCF corps (Sea Cadet Corps, New Zealand Cadet Corps, and Air Training Corps).
Leadership Status
The WOCA holds an advisory leadership role and exercises influence through established command and staff channels rather than direct command authority.
Reporting & Relationships
The WOCA reports to the Area Coordinator (Central) and works closely with Area Support Officers, senior NZCF staff, and the Warrant Officer Cadet Forces.
Appointment & Eligibility
The position is open to experienced Cadet Warrant Officers (CDTWO) who have completed at least nine months as a Unit Warrant Officer. Candidates must demonstrate strong leadership, communication skills, and the capacity to support cadet activities across a broad geographic area.
The WOCA is typically appointed for fixed term of up to two years, and is posted to the strength of the CA CFTSU. While the role does not require residence in a major centre, regular liaison with Area staff is expected.
Purpose & Significance
The WOCA plays a key role in shaping the cadet experience at a regional and national level. The position provides opportunities to:
* Influence the operation and development of the New Zealand Cadet Forces.
* Represent cadet views to senior officers and contribute to decisions affecting all NZCF personnel.
* Gain exposure to organisational, operational, and strategic functions within the NZCF.
* Engage with leadership at a national level and develop advanced leadership skills.
